name: First Results from KamLAND: Evidence for Reactor Anti-Neutrino Disappearance

date.note: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 021802 (2003); date recorded here is the preprint submission date, see `date_kind`.

title: First Results from KamLAND: Evidence for Reactor Anti-Neutrino Disappearance

claim.quote: First Results from KamLAND: Evidence for Reactor Anti-Neutrino Disappearance

summary.plain: KamLAND's first data showed fewer antineutrinos arriving from distant Japanese reactors than expected if nothing happened to them on the way — direct proof, from reactors rather than the Sun, that the 'large mixing angle' explanation of the solar neutrino problem is right.
summary.technical: In a 162 ton·yr (145.1-day) exposure, KamLAND measured a ratio of observed to expected reactor antineutrino events of 0.611±0.085(stat)±0.041(syst) for E>3.4 MeV, excluding no-oscillation at 99.95% CL and, with CPT invariance, favouring the Large Mixing Angle solution to the solar neutrino problem over other two-flavour oscillation solutions.

why_it_matters.value: In the context of two-flavor oscillations with CPT invariance, the first KamLAND data exclude every oscillation solution to the solar neutrino problem except the Large Mixing Angle solution, using reactor antineutrinos.
why_it_matters.quote: these results exclude all oscillation solutions but the ‘Large Mixing Angle’ solution to the solar neutrino problem using reactor ν̄e sources

significance.quote: The deficit of events is inconsistent with the expected rate for standard ν̄e propagation at the 99.95% confidence level
significance.note: Not expressed as a sigma value in the fetched abstract; recorded as the stated confidence level.
